name: Bake Street
note: Bakery-café doing fried chicken buns and weekend specials. Order the Nashville hot chicken bun.
maps_query: Bake Street Rectory Road / Clapton London N16

name: Spence Bakery
note: Church Street sourdough bakery with sandwiches. Get a pain au chocolat and coffee.
maps_query: Spence Bakery Stoke Newington London N16

name: Roti Stop
note: Tiny Caribbean corner takeaway. Order curry goat in flaky roti with channa, and peanut punch.
maps_query: Roti Stop Stamford Hill / Stoke Newington London N16

name: Jolene
note: Cult bakery-restaurant milling its own grain. Get a croissant or palmier from the counter.

name: Raab's The Bakers
note: Old-school family bakery with filled baps. Get the birthday cake slice, under £2.
maps_query: Raab's The Bakers Islington (Essex Road) London N1

name: Zeit für Brot
note: Berlin bakery's London outpost. Order the currywurst sausage roll and an apple-cinnamon schnecke.
maps_query: Zeit für Brot Angel London N1

name: Pophams
note: The original branch of the inventive laminated-pastry bakery. Get a signature seasonal pastry.

name: OISO Korean Street Food
note: Family-run Korean café with a short menu. Order the bibimbap or bulgogi.
maps_query: OISO Korean Street Food King's Cross (Caledonian Road) London N1

name: Johnny Schnitzel
note: Schnitzel sandwich specialist. Order the schnitzel sandwich.
maps_query: Johnny Schnitzel King's Cross / Clerkenwell London WC1X

name: Max's Sandwich Shop
note: Max Halley's maximalist sandwich shop. Order Ham, Egg 'n' Chips.
maps_query: Max's Sandwich Shop Stroud Green / Finsbury Park London N4

name: Baban's Naan
note: Hole-in-the-wall tandoor naan shop at knockdown prices. Get the cheese or za'atar naan.
maps_query: Baban's Naan Finsbury Park (Blackstock Road) London N4

name: Dilara
note: Uyghur canteen doing hand-pulled noodles and dumplings. Order the beef hand-pulled noodles.
maps_query: Dilara Finsbury Park (Blackstock Road) London N4

name: The Happening Bagel Bakery
note: Old-school bagel bakery. Get a bagel, and a challah to take home.
maps_query: The Happening Bagel Bakery Finsbury Park (Seven Sisters Road) London N4

name: Fink's
note: Neighbourhood deli-café doing sandwiches, coffee and provisions. Order a sandwich and a flat white.

name: Three Uncles
note: Hong Kong roast-meat counter. Order char siu with lo mein noodles.
maps_query: Three Uncles Camden (Hawley Wharf) London NW1
tip: Top floor of the Hawley Wharf food hall

name: Holy Sheep
note: Build-your-own Yunnan rice-noodle bowls. Go mala broth with dried beancurd roll.
maps_query: Holy Sheep Camden (Hawley Wharf) London NW1

name: Kossoff's
note: Bakery on a site that's been a bakery since the 1920s. Order a croissant cup, or the focaccia at lunch.

name: Crunch
note: Ten-seat sandwich counter using thick buttery brioche. Order the patty melt with caramelised onions.
tip: Tiny room, but the queue moves fast

name: Paul Rothe & Son
note: Old-school family deli making plain white-bread sandwiches. Get the egg mayo, with anchovy if you like.
maps_query: Paul Rothe & Son Marylebone London W1U

name: Panadera
note: Filipino bakery doing pandesal, ube bakes and sandos. The corned beef hash sando is the order.
tip: Soho branch queues are long at weekends

name: Arôme Bakery
note: French-Asian bakery on Mercer Street. The thick honey butter toast is the cult item.
maps_query: Arôme Bakery Covent Garden London WC2H

name: Fortitude Bakehouse
note: Tiny bakery in the Colonnade mews with excellent buns and pastries. Get the beignet or the kouign-amann.

name: Bageriet
note: Tiny Swedish bakery on Rose Street with fika classics. Order a cardamom or cinnamon bun.

name: Miel Bakery
note: Warren Street patisserie with excellent small bakes. Get the pistachio financier and a double chocolate cookie.

name: Fred Bakery
note: Bun specialist near Oxford Circus. Get a cinnamon bun served warm, or the tiramisu bun.

name: Banh Mi Aha!
note: Lamb's Conduit Street takeaway making proper Vietnamese baguettes. The special bánh mì is the order.
maps_query: Banh Mi Aha! Bloomsbury London WC1N

name: Maison Bertaux
note: London's oldest French patisserie, a Greek Street fixture since 1871. Get the mille-feuille or the strawberry tart.

name: Beigel Bake
note: Round-the-clock Brick Lane bagel bakery. The hot salt beef beigel with mustard and gherkin is the one.
maps_query: Beigel Bake Brick Lane London E1
tip: Open 24 hours; expect a queue late at night

name: Banh Mi Kêu Deli
note: Old Street bánh mì counter that has run for years. Get the classic, or the Hoi An Deluxe.
maps_query: Banh Mi Kêu Deli Shoreditch London EC1V

name: Cafe Mondo
note: Sandwich bar from the Mondo Sando team. Get the turkey with chipotle butter, or pork and provolone.

name: Guacamoles
note: Taqueria inside Rye Lane Indoor Market with free guac and salsa. Birria tacos are the standout.

name: Silk Road
note: Uyghur canteen open since 2008. Order the hand-pulled noodles and cumin lamb skewers.

name: Funchal Bakery
note: Portuguese bakery and caff with one of London's best pastéis de nata. Add a salt cod fritter.

name: Aries Bakehouse
note: Acre Lane bakery with inventive pastries and good sourdough. Try the jerk chicken sausage roll.

name: Milk Run
note: Bakery from Balham café Milk, with croissants, danishes and toasties. Get a danish with a flat white.
maps_query: Milk Run Balham / Tooting Bec London SW17

name: Maya's Bakehouse
note: Neighbourhood bakery with sourdough and seasonal bakes. Get the spiced bun or the Guinness cake.
maps_query: Maya's Bakehouse Tulse Hill London SW2

name: Eric's
note: Serious little bakery on Upland Road. The croissants are the reason to go; also try the coffee custard morning bun.

name: Lulu's
note: Deli by day, wine bar by night. Get the mortadella, pistachio and rocket ciabatta at lunch.

name: M. Manze
note: Tiled pie and mash shop open since 1902. Order pie, mash and liquor, then the ice cream.

name: The Beefsteaks
note: Market stall grilling British bavette. Get the steak sarnie with watercress and onion marmalade.
maps_query: The Beefsteaks Bermondsey (Maltby Street Market) London SE1
tip: Weekends only at Maltby Street Market

name: Daddy Bao
note: Tiny Taiwanese bao bar from the Mr Bao family. Get the pork belly bao and the fried chicken.
tip: Very small; book or expect a wait

name: Tooting Market
note: Covered market full of small stalls. Get Pepi's Guyanese saltfish bake, or jerk chicken from The Lone Fisherman.
tip: Each stall keeps its own hours

name: Sam Sandwiches
note: Algerian street-food sandwiches loaded with chips, fried egg and harissa. Get the minced beef sandwich.
maps_query: Sam Sandwiches Shepherd's Bush Market London W12

name: Mr Falafel
note: Palestinian falafel stall with about a dozen wraps. Get the deluxe, with fried cauliflower and crispy potato.
maps_query: Mr Falafel Shepherd's Bush Market London W12

name: Secret Sandwich Shop
note: Japanese-style sandos on soft milk bread. Get the tuna mayo with salt and vinegar crisps added.
maps_query: Secret Sandwich Shop Notting Hill London W11

name: Layla Bakery
note: Portobello Road bakery with inventive pastries. The strawberry jam and cream bow tie is the order.
maps_query: Layla Bakery Notting Hill London W10

name: Kuro Bakery
note: Japanese-leaning bakery doing shokupan and filled bagels. Get the croissant bread and butter pudding.
maps_query: Kuro Bakery Notting Hill London W11

name: Happy Sky Bakery
note: Small Japanese bakery known for milk loaves. Get a sando, or a matcha mochi bow.
maps_query: Happy Sky Bakery Askew Road London W12

name: Tacos MX
note: Takeaway taco window on Lillie Road. The Baja fish taco is the one to order.
tip: About 15 minutes' wait; very little seating
